cards.text: Israel's camped at Kadesh, and Moses sends messengers to the king of Edom. Here's the thing: the Edomites come from Esau (Genesis 36:9), and Esau's brother was Jacob, the one God renamed Israel (Genesis 32:28). So this isn't a message to strangers, friend. This is family.

cards.question: Knowing that family history, how does the message to Edom's king begin? "This is what your ___ Israel says"

cards.text: Then the message walks back through all the hardship Israel's been through. Their fathers went down to Egypt and lived there many years.

cards.question: Israel's message to Edom says the Egyptians treated Israel's fathers kindly.
The message says Israel cried out to the LORD, and He heard their voice. What did He send to bring them out of Egypt?

cards.text: Then they get to the point: "Now look, we are in Kadesh, a city on the edge of your territory." It's like texting your neighbor from the sidewalk before you cut across their yard.

cards.question: Israel's camped right at the edge of Edom. What does the message ask Edom's king for?
Israel promises Edom they won't go through any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well.
Israel also promises to stay on one road through Edom, not turning to the right or to the left. Which road?

cards.text: Friend, they're promising to walk through Edom like somebody tiptoeing past a sleeping baby. STRAIGHT LINE. Then Edom answers.

cards.question: Israel asked so carefully. What does Edom answer?

answers.text: No or they'll come out with the sword
Yes if Israel pays a toll first
Yes but only through the desert

cards.text: Israel doesn't take that first no. That was me every time the drawer opened: "OVER HERE! I've still got a few good stamps in me!"

cards.question: Israel says they'll stay on the main road, and if they or their herds drink Edom's water, they'll ___ for it.
In Israel's second offer, they ask Edom only to let them pass through on foot.

cards.text: Edom insists: "You may not pass through." Five words. No sorry. No maybe next time.

cards.question: After telling Israel no a second time, what does Edom do?

answers.text: They come out with a large army
They send gifts out to Moses

cards.text: Two polite asks. Two no's. And a whole army standing at the border. Edom refuses to let Israel pass through their territory.

cards.question: With Edom's army out, Israel fights its way through Edom's territory.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 2 quotes "This is what your ___ Israel says", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: "Israel's camped at Kadesh...", "Here's the thing...", "So this isn't a message to strangers, friend." and "This is family." The limit is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: Card 1 gives away the answer to card 2. It says Esau's brother was Jacob, who was renamed Israel, and then "This is family." After that, the blank in "This is what your ___ Israel says" can only be "brother."

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Moses appears here for the first time, but the card doesn't say who he is (for example, "Moses, Israel's leader").

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Both wrong answers are things God really used to bring Israel out of Egypt. The pillar of fire is in Exodus 13:21, and the strong east wind that parted the sea is in Exodus 14:21. A baker could argue that "A pillar of fire" or "A great wind" is a right answer to "What did He send to bring them out of Egypt?"

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The joke compares Israel to texting a neighbor "before you cut across their yard." That gives away card 7's answer (permission to pass through) and rules out the wrong answers "A place to settle down" and "Soldiers to march with them."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card cites only Numbers 20:18. Its first sentence retells the promises from 20:17 (walking through carefully in a straight line). The citation should be Numbers 20:17-18. The 20:17 material also repeats what cards 8 and 9 just covered.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: "Friend, they're promising...", "STRAIGHT LINE." and "Then Edom answers."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new habit for Papa Dorin's time in the drawer: shouting "OVER HERE!" every time it opened. That adds to his backstory, and it conflicts with it. The backstory says he went quiet for a while and that everyone in the drawer held their breath together when it opened.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't have the same core action. Israel answers a refusal with a better offer. Papa Dorin shouting to get noticed in the drawer comes after no refusal and involves no offer.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: Edom's quote, "Five words.", "No sorry." and "No maybe next time."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences. The first three ("Two polite asks. Two no's. And a whole army standing at the border.") recap 20:18-20, which cards 11, 15 and 16 already covered. Only the last sentence moves the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
